Description: Sites that provide information on or promote mass entertainment media such as theatre, amusement parks, music, comics, fan clubs, and so on.
Sites that promote music for entertainment purposes related to bands, orchestras, festivals, and so on. It also includes audio streaming websites.
Sites that report information or commentary on current events or contemporary issues, including newspapers, news wire services, news magazines, and radio news stations.
Other sites related to entertainment/recreation that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites that offer streaming or downloadable radio programming.
Sites related to television programming or movies.
Sites that are related to streaming video.
Sites that provide service links, banners, or ads for websites.
Sites related to online journals, diaries, or newsletters that express personal thoughts/opinions about internet, social, or political issues.
Sites that use content delivery networks to optimize the delivery of localized content to end users.
Sites that display advertisements for sale or purchase of goods and services. It also includes sites like the marriage bureau, etc.
Sites related to institutions and colleges offering formal courses of advanced studies for adults.
Sites that offer corporate and product information but do not sell products.

Sites that provide tools used by developers for coding, debugging, testing and managing software projects. This category includes websites and online platforms related to software development, programming and IT infrastructure.
Sites related to Usenet, Usenet news, forums, newsgroups, or online bulletin board systems.
Sites that provide DNS resolution over an encrypted and secure connection with the DNS over HTTPS service. This category includes DNS server URLs that support DNS resolution using the HTTPS protocol.
Sites and services that allow users to convert files from one format to another.
Sites that offer hosting, backup, and sharing of files on the Internet.
Sites that provide information related to financial investment and firms that offer financial services. It doesn't include websites that are related to insurance.

Sites that offer non-generative AI and ML applications and services. This category include websites for AI research labs, AI-powered solution providers, AI/ML app demonstrations and tutorials, and that enable automation with AI and ML.
Sites that provide tools, services, or information related to generative AI (i.e., a subfield of artificial intelligence that can generate new text, images, videos, or audio.).
Sites that offer a systematic recording of past events or analysis and commentary on causes and effects, motives, or connections relating to events.
Sites that provide video or image hosting, linking, and/or sharing.

Sites that allow users to compare and buy insurance policies and resources explaining specific types of insurance (e.g., life insurance, health insurance). This category include company websites that provide self-service options for managing policies.
Sites that offer online utility applications or services that assist in internet communication.
Sites that provide employment services, assistance in finding employment, or tools for locating employers.
Sites related to the education of children.
Sites that offer access to, software for, or participation in any internet chat forum. Chat is defined as any online conversation taking place in real-time.
Sites that provide trading of securities and management of investment assets. It also includes sites that offer financial investment strategies, quotes, and news.
Sites and links that are used for downloading operating systems such as Windows, iOS, etc. and software updates.
Other sites related to business and economy that are not classified in any of the defined categories.
Other sites related to education that are not included in the defined categories.
Other sites related to information technology that are not included in the defined categories.
Other sites related to internet communications that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites that provide client software to enable peer-to-peer file sharing and transfers.
Sites that offer multiple web-based services to assist a user's experience on the internet.
Sites that provide information about or are related to the sale and delivery of technical and professional services.
Sites that offers scholars and academics source documents and research assistance.
Sites that provide information or software to enable authorized access to a desktop computer or private network from a remote location.
Sites that provide Internet search services geared specifically for families and children and prevent discovery of objectionable material.
Sites related to education in science and technology.

Description: Sites that are related to or offer downloading of large number of legal third party software.
Sites that offer translation services for web pages, URLs, or other text strings.
Sites that assist in conducting video conferencing or provide software to enable virtual meetings.
Sites that offer web hosting services, as well as domain names and web space, to host end user web pages.
Sites that offer search services for the internet, indices, and directories.
Sites that provide email accounts, free or otherwise.
This category includes IP addresses owned by Zscaler's data centers and services such as IP addresses of the Public Service Edge on a cloud and global VIP service.
Sites related to governments and their agencies or militaries.
Sites related to military or armed forces, excluding those that discuss or sell weapons.
Sites that have not yet been classified.

Sites whose domains were created in the last 30 days and are currently not categorized by Zscaler. This category also includes domains that we encounter for the first time. Domains under this category are considered suspicious until they are categorized or better understood by Zscaler.

Sites that Zscaler has not been able to categorize. Some of the reasons a site may appear here are that the site is a login page without any other details, it no longer exists, or it is unresolvable on the internet
Other sites related to government and politics that are not included in the defined categories.
Other sites that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites related to, or sponsored by, organizations that seek to influence viewpoints, change or reform public policy, public opinion, or government practices.
Sites related to travel planning, information, or activities, including reservation services, destination listings, and special event promotion.
Sites that provide information about or promote vehicles, or offer for purchase vehicle parts or maintenance.
Sites related to sex education and targeted at adult readers.
Sites related to adult content not covered by more specific categories, for example, penile enlargement, erectile dysfunction, adult entertainment, and so on.
Sites that allow users to surf the Internet and/or send email anonymously by providing proxy bypass functionality or information or instructions on how to do so.
Sites that provide information about artistic sexual expression or information about or images of body piercing, tattoos, and any form of body art.
Sites related to the promotion of illegal tools and mechanisms to crack passwords, generate and distribute malicious software, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems.
Sites related to bootlegged or otherwise illegally available copyrighted material, such as program, DVD movies, and CD or MP3 music.
Sites that provide online gambling or are related to gambling assistance, training information, or advocacy.
Sites associated with sex education for children, including sites that offer information about sex, human reproduction, or any other sexually oriented material used to educate.
Sites that display or are dedicated to lingerie or swimsuits that could be considered inappropriate for teenagers and younger children.

Sites that promote or discuss the cultivation, manufacture, distribution or sale of marijuana for recreational or medicinal purposes. It includes web pages on legalizing marijuana, using marijuana for medicinal purposes, marijuana facts and info pages, and sites that mention hemp, cannabis, blunts, panama red, etc.
Sites that contain humor and mature themes unsuitable for teenagers and children, but no pornography or strong profanity.
Sites that promote divisive rhetoric or action, describe certain populations as dangerous or evil, or promote intolerance of individuals or groups.
Sites that provide either artistic or non-artistic nude images in any medium (sculpture, photographs, paintings, and so on).
Other sites related to adult material that are not in the defined categories.
Sites associated with the use or advocacy of illegal drugs or the illegal use of prescribed drugs, except those sites related to Marijuana.
Other sites related to illegal or questionable activities that are not classified in the defined categories.
Sites related to soft- and/or hard-core pornography, regardless of medium (written, images, movies, and so on).
Sites that contain generally acknowledged profanity but do not fall under a more specific category such as "Pornography."
Sites that are generally related to illegal activities but do not fall under a more specific category.
Sites that provide social networking for adults, such as dating sites.
Sites that contain crude or offensive content.
Sites that depict, promote, or feature violence.
Sites that promote the use, making, or distribution of weapons.
Sites that use custom encryption for protecting users’ data. Zscaler can inspect the HTTP headers of such sites but not the body content.
Sites that dynamically update the IP address of the hostname and provide DNS resolution. This category includes DNS server URLs that support Dynamic DNS resolution.
Sites whose domains were reactivated after a brief period of inactivity for about 10 days. Some of these websites were once active with a legitimate reputation.
Other sites related to security that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites that are known to distribute or contain code that displays unwanted advertisements or that gathers user information without the user’s knowledge.
Sites related to the use of alcohol and tobacco products, excluding those that inform on the hazards of alcohol and tobacco.
Sites related to nontraditional or nonreligious spiritual belief systems, or related to the practice or advocacy of affecting events through supernatural means.
Sites related to the mores, activities, organizations, and collective behavior of peoples that define various cultures around the world.
Sites related to groups or movements whose membership is marked by zeal, passion, and obedience to a degree generally considered excessive by the mainstream.
Sites that list, discuss, review, advertise, or promote dining and restaurants.
Sites related to issues specific to the family such as divorce, adoption, infertility, domestic violence, and so on.
Sites related to an individual’s physical and mental well-being.
Sites related to hobbies and leisure, or pursuits or interests engaged in for pleasure and relaxation.
Sites related to lifestyle activities such as parties and so on for all orientations.
Sites related to online games and other websites related to games that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites that offer participation in online auctions or support the offer and purchase of goods between individuals.
Sites that provide, or advertise ways to purchase products or services over the Internet or by telephone.
Other sites related to religion that is not classified in the defined categories.
Other sites related to shopping and auctions that are not included in the defined categories.
Other sites related to social and family issues that are not classified in the defined categories.
Other sites related to society and lifestyle that are not included in the defined categories.
Sites that offer information or services related to buying, selling, renting, or financing property.
Sites related to issues generally considered to engender controversies, such as abortion, euthanasia, legalization of drugs, and so on.
Sites that enable the creation of online communities or the facilitation of personal introductions, dating, and networking.
Sites that reside on social networking sites and contain material that would otherwise merit categorization into the Games category.
Sites related to charitable organizations, community or environmental interest groups, or social advocacy.
Sites related to sports or recreation.
Sites related to traditionally organized religious activities, participation, and belief.

Class: Note: The categories under the Advanced Security super-category apply only to Advanced Threat Protection policy.

Description: Sites that contain adware or spyware. Adware displays malicious advertisements that can collect users' information without their knowledge.

Sites that contain software designed to communicate periodically with a "command and control" center, and a master application instructs the infected computers to send spam, phishing email, or perform other malicious tasks.
Sites that allow cryptocurrency mining network traffic and scripts.
Sites that attempt to download dangerous content to your browser when you visit them. This includes vulnerable ActiveX controls and web browsers that are known to have been exploited.
Sites that provide P2P file sharing, P2P anonymizer, and P2P VoIP.
Sites that mimic legitimate banking and financial sites (e.g., Citibank.com, PayPal.com, etc.).
Sites that gather users' information without notification and sell this information to advertisers or criminals.
Sites that pretend to contain useful information, to get higher ranking in search engine results or drive traffic to phishing, adware, or spyware distribution sites.
Sites with known web browser vulnerabilities that can be exploited. This includes exploits for Internet Explorer and Adobe Flash.
Sites that allow malicious users to inject their own code into it. This includes cookie stealing and potentially malicious requests.
Sites that contain malicious contents such as injected scripts, vulnerable ActiveX, zero-pixel iFrames, etc.

Sites that provide suspicious destinations protection. This includes requests to any country in the world based on ISO3166 mapping of countries to their IP address space. Websites are blocked based on the location of the web server.
Sites that provide unauthorized communication protection. This includes IRC tunneling applications, SSH tunneling applications, and anonymizer sites that are used to bypass firewalls and proxies.
